title: PaCELab Equip: Shared Laboratory Equipment System
summary: A PHP and SQLite web application that records equipment use in a shared laboratory, charges each use to a grant account, prevents scheduling conflicts, and produces the monthly charge report for the business office.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 for the drive copy; the bundled PHP in tools\php runs it, so nothing else is installed
On a campus server: PHP 8.0 or later with pdo_sqlite (or pdo_pgsql for PostgreSQL) and a folder the web server can write to
install: Plug in the drive and open the application folder under apps\pacelab-equip.

Double-click SETUP.bat. It creates config.local.json, points the data folder at ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\data, then runs SETUP ON THIS PC.bat, which adds the logon and Desktop shortcuts for this folder and starts the server.
run: Double-click the Shared Lab Equipment shortcut on the Desktop (no window) or START HERE.bat. Either starts the server when it is down and opens the browser.
STOP SERVER.bat stops this application's server and nothing else. RUN TESTS.bat runs the regression suite against a scratch database.

settings.meaning: The folder holding lab.sqlite, the installer lock and the logs, relative to the application folder: ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\data on the drive. Empty means data\ inside the application folder.
Where the daily backups go, relative to the application folder: ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\backups on the drive.
On a server only, in the environment (env.template.txt lists them): pgsql and the PostgreSQL connection. Unset means SQLite.

data: The database lives outside the application folder, in data\pacelab-equip\data on the drive, named by config.local.json. It is never stored in git. Without config.local.json the application uses data\ in its own folder, as it always did.
backups: While the server runs, the supervisor takes one backup a day with SQLite's VACUUM INTO, reads it back and counts its rows, and keeps 60 days in data\pacelab-equip\backups. BACK UP NOW.bat takes one on demand and proves it restores.
